took_what: Claimed the item BEFORE doing any work (lesson taken directly from CYC-0024's two live id/claim collisions this session) and closed the single-slot-artifact hazard's remaining gap in research/modalities/atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py. A CLI-level refusal (a foreign --series argument is rejected before it reaches the fetch half) already existed from an earlier fix; this item's gap was different -- a restore that swaps the INPUTS CACHE and the ARTIFACT together, both self-consistently describing the wrong GEO series, with no --series argument involved at all. That is exactly what happened 2026-08-07 (325258cb8): GSE28866 overwrote GSE299349 and went undetected for three weeks, because the derive-reproduces check (main()'s default/--check path) only asks whether the artifact reproduces from its own cache, never whether that cache is for the series the module's SOURCE says it is.
fix_applied: research/modalities/atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py: main() now compares the committed artifact's own `series` field against the module-level SERIES constant BEFORE the derive-reproduces comparison, failing with a named SERIES MISMATCH diagnostic (and a re-fetch instruction) even when fresh == committed. SERIES lives in this .py file, which a data-only restore does not touch, so it is the one thing such a restore cannot silently carry backwards along with the data it does revert.
